cards.explanation: The answer is that the LORD will restore their splendor. "For the LORD will restore the splendor of Jacob like the splendor of Israel…" (Nahum 2:2). Destroyers had laid them waste and ruined the branches of their vine, and the LORD says He will restore them anyway. Right in the middle of a loud, scary scene, Nahum slips in a promise, friends.

The answer is torches, friends! The chariots are "…appearing like torches, darting about like lightning." (Nahum 2:4). They dash through the streets and rush around the plazas. I'd hate to be the one standing in a crosswalk there.

The answer is True! "The river gates are thrown open and the palace collapses." (Nahum 2:6). Nahum says it in one short sentence, and I think that makes it hit harder. The gates open, and the palace falls. Both of those are in that one verse.

The answer is that the city be exiled and carried away, friends. "It is decreed that the city be exiled and carried away…" (Nahum 2:7). The palace has fallen, and now the city itself is carried off. I think that's a big change for a city that felt so settled.

The answer is that it is draining away, friends. "Nineveh has been like a pool of water throughout her days, but now it is draining away." (Nahum 2:8). Then the city's people cry, "Stop! Stop!" but no one turns back. That's a pool going dry, and nobody is able to stop it.

The answer is True. Nahum writes, "Stop! Stop!" and then "…but no one turns back." (Nahum 2:8). The cry goes out as the pool drains. People are calling out, and nobody turns around. I think that's a sad scene.

The answer is False. Nahum says, "There is no end to the treasure, an abundance of every precious thing." (Nahum 2:9). The verse has the cry, "Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold!" Then Nahum says, "She is emptied! Yes, she is desolate and laid waste!" (Nahum 2:10).

The answer is emptied and laid waste, friends. "She is emptied! Yes, she is desolate and laid waste!" (Nahum 2:10). After all that plundering, the city is left bare. Emptied is the first word he uses. Nahum puts it plainly.

The answer is True! "Hearts melt, knees knock, bodies tremble, and every face grows pale!" (Nahum 2:10). Nahum piles one reaction on another. Knees knocking and pale faces are both in the verse. I think anybody would know that feeling.

The answer is enough to fill its dens, friends. "The lion mauled enough for its cubs and strangled prey for the lioness. It filled its dens with the kill, and its lairs with mauled prey." (Nahum 2:12). It's a picture of a lion with its dens full. I think it's heavy, so I'll say it once and move on.

The answer is against, friends. "Behold, I am against you…" declares the LORD of Hosts (Nahum 2:13). The LORD speaks plainly, and there's no way to misread it. After all the pictures in this chapter, here is His own voice.

The answer is the voices of her messengers, friends. The LORD says, "…the voices of your messengers will no longer be heard." (Nahum 2:13). He says it last, after the chariots, the young lions and the prey. Those voices go quiet.
